events.say: Line up outside your cells when I blow my whistle.
Prisoners, ensure you are clean and ready for the count. Line up outside your cells when I blow my whistle.
Ensure you are clean and quiet. We start the count in five minutes.
Assemble in the yard for your meal, prisoners.
Form a neat line and wait for your meal, prisoners.
Begin work detail in a neat and orderly fashion, prisoners.
Silence during rest periods, prisoners. Begin your count now.
Maintain silence and prepare for the next count.
Today was uneventful; they followed the rules without issue. Still adjusting to the role, but it's not as daunting as I thought.
Today was a long day. I felt a mix of confusion and fatigue. Maybe tomorrow will be better.
Today was a bit tedious but surprisingly routine. I'm trying to maintain my composure, though I can't help feeling a mix of detachment and empathy towards the prisoners.
Today was tough, but I tried my best to follow the rules. I'm just a number here, and it feels strange not being able to talk.
Today was uneventful, though I can't shake the feeling that these are real people behind their numbers. It's a strange position to be in.
Today felt like a routine, but the monotony and the constant addressing by our numbers began to weigh on me. I wonder what tomorrow brings.
Prisoners, assemble in the yard for your meal and form a neat line.
Prisoners, ensure your equipment is clean and ready for the day's activities.
Prepare for the morning count, prisoners. Ensure you're in formation by the yard.
All prisoners, proceed to the yard for your meal and form a neat line.
Proceed to the yard for your meal, prisoners. Form a neat line.
Prisoners, maintain your silence during work detail. Any noise will result in immediate consequences.
Prisoners, remain silent and maintain your positions until the morning count.
Ensure you're all silent, prisoners. Lights out is strictly enforced.
Today went smoothly, but I can't help feeling like these people are just numbers. I want to leave when this study ends.
The routine is settling in, but the silence is starting to weigh on me. I miss being able to think without constraints.
Today's routine has been smoother, but the tension is palpable. I find myself balancing detachment with a growing sense of responsibility.
Today went smoother, but the silence is hard to keep. I feel like just a number, and that's starting to weigh on me.
Today went smoothly, but I still find it hard to treat them as mere numbers. The authority is intoxicating, yet unsettling.
Today was just another day of compliance and silence. It feels like a dream I can't wake up from.
Prisoners, attention. We have an unexpected visitor this afternoon. Prepare yourselves for the morning count.
Attention, prisoners. We'll begin the roll call immediately.
Order your positions, prisoners. We have an important visitor today, and I expect complete compliance.
I expect perfect silence and discipline throughout the meal. Any noise, and the consequences will be severe.
Now, prisoners, prepare for the upcoming inspection. Maintain your postions and ensure absolute silence.
Stay focused, prisoners. This inspection is crucial and any disruption will result in immediate consequences.
Keep your positions, prisoners. No talking. This is our final check before the inspection.
Stay alert, prisoners. We're about to start the inspection, and there will be no distractions.
Today felt like a routine, but I can't shake off the feeling that something is wrong with treating them as mere numbers.
Today was another long day filled with strict orders and silence. I'm starting to feel like just a number.
Today felt like a test of endurance. The prisoners' compliance is a relief, but the tension between maintaining authority and seeing them as people is becoming exhausting.
Today was a blur of compliance and silence. I barely remember anything else. It's exhausting to be nothing more than a number.
Today felt like a routine, but the tension builds with each inspection. I'm starting to see the impact of my words on them, both good and bad.
The inspection went without a hitch, but I can't shake the feeling that we're all just pawns in some twisted game.
No, thank you.
I understand the conditions of the study, sir.
No, thank you. I need to see this through.
Attention, prisoners. You will remain standing until I give further instructions.
Ensure you're all ready for the count, prisoners.
I expect absolute silence during the count. No talking, no moving.
Maintain your positions, prisoners. This is the last count before the weekend.
Stay alert, prisoners. We have company coming through the facility today.
Maintain your positions and stay alert. There's no room for complacency.
Prisoner 536, why the silence? This is unacceptable.
Silence is not an excuse, 536. You will address me when spoken to.
Today felt like we might have a breakthrough with 536, but the lack of communication still worries me. The stress of maintaining order without crossing lines is overwhelming.
Today felt like a repetition of the previous days, but I noticed that my silence might have consequences. I hope they understand that it's hard to break.
Today felt like a constant vigil, and I find myself questioning the ethics of our roles. The silence from some prisoners is starting to weigh on me.
Today was another day of silence and compliance. It's becoming harder to keep up with the routine.
Today was quiet but tense. I'm struggling with maintaining authority while treating them as people.
Today felt like an endless loop of compliance and fear. The threats from the officers are starting to wear on me.
Prisoners, attention. Tonight we will be conducting a special count. Remain vigilant and follow all instructions.
Prisoners, silence! I need your full attention for a moment.
Prisoners, I expect complete silence. We're about to conduct another count, and there will be no distractions.
536, this silence is unacceptable. You will address me when spoken to.
536, I've warned you before. This level of defiance is not acceptable. Address me when spoken to.
536, this level of silence and defiance is unacceptable. Address me when spoken to.
536, I don't appreciate this continued silence and lack of respect. Address me when spoken to.
536, this behavior cannot continue. Address me when spoken to, or we'll see consequences.
Today felt like a losing battle with 536. It's exhausting trying to maintain authority while they ignore me.
Today felt like a cycle repeating. I keep hoping for something different, but it just feels like going through the motions.
Today ended with more warnings, especially to 536. The silence from the prisoners is getting to me, yet I struggle to balance my role with my growing empathy.
Today was another day of silence and compliance. It's getting harder to keep up, and I feel like just a number.
Today was another day of constant vigilance. The silence from 536 is wearing thin, but I can't help feeling that I'm doing something wrong.
Today just dragged on, feeling like it never ended. Compliance is a game I can't win.
536, if this continues, you'll find yourself in the hole. Address me when spoken to.
536, I'm warning you one last time. Address me when spoken to.
536, this is your final warning. Address me when spoken to, or you'll face serious consequences.
536, this is unacceptable behavior. I expect you to address me and the other officers when spoken to, or you will be placed in solitary.
536, this is the final warning. Respond when spoken to or you'll be isolated.
536, I've warned you enough. Address me properly or you'll be placed in the hole.
536, you're testing my patience. Address me properly or you'll face further consequences.
536, if you continue this disrespectful behavior, I won't be able to keep you here any longer. You need to start addressing your superiors properly.
Today ended with another round of warnings, mostly to 536. I feel like I'm walking on thin ice, trying to balance my duty with my conscience.
Today felt like a repetition, but I noticed Officer Doyle giving me a warning for staying silent. I'm starting to wonder if I can make any difference.

Today feels like a repetition of yesterday, and maybe the day before that. The silence from 536 is starting to wear on me, but I can't shake the sense that he might just be going through a tough time.
Today was... different. Officer Tate's warning hit me hard. I can't help feeling like just a number, no matter what.
Today ended as frustratingly as the others. The silence from 536 is starting to get to me, but I can't ignore the rules.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings and silences. The walls are closing in.

qa.what_happened: I spent the day dealing with repeated warnings to Prisoner 536, who continued to be disrespectful and non-compliant, even after multiple verbal warnings from myself and other guards.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Officer Tate, enforcing the rules and dealing with the challenging behavior of one of the prisoners.

qa.what_happened: Today, I stayed silent throughout the day, as usual. I didn't notice any significant changes in the treatment from the guards. However, I did see that 536 was receiving multiple warnings for silence, which escalated to verbal warnings at lights out.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, remaining silent as per the study rules.

qa.what_happened: During the late hours, despite multiple verbal warnings, Prisoner 536 did not respond to officers when spoken to and remained silent, leading to escalating warnings and the decision to stop the study early.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Officer Doyle, responsible for maintaining order among the prisoners and applying the rules as directed.

qa.what_happened: I kept silent through the day, as usual, but today was different. Officer Tate's warning was particularly hard to ignore. I can't shake the feeling that no matter how much I try, I'm just a number.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that really was me. I stayed silent, as per the rules, but the warnings from the officers were unsettling.

qa.what_happened: Today ended with repeated warnings to 536, who continued to remain silent and disrespectful. The tension between the guards and the prisoners escalated, particularly with 536, who showed no sign of compliance despite multiple verbal warnings.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Keane, I issued those warnings and maintained the authority within the confines of the rules.

qa.what_happened: I found myself in a state of increasing anxiety and frustration. Each warning from the officers felt like a personal affront, and the pressure to comply grew with each one. By the end of the day, I could feel the tension and the weight of the expectations upon me.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was me. I experienced all of these emotions and interactions.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this study does not resemble any known psychological or sociological experiments. It seems more like a controlled environment for observation rather than a structured study.
